item.title: FAT Filesystems
item.description: The File Allocation Table (FAT) family began on small Microsoft systems and became the interchange format for DOS and IBM PC media. Simple data structures made FAT practical in boot firmware and constrained operating systems. The same design omits journaling, ownership, and transaction semantics, so interoperability rather than failure isolation explains its continued use.
